newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Creech nominates FEC committee members.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Creech nominates FEC committee members.

text.p: Leader of the House Wyatt Creech has tabled 17 notices of motion to be debated on Tuesday setting up the New Zealand parliament's select committees and nominating the MPs to sit on them.

The 12 nominations for the powerful finance and expenditure select committee (FEC) are: Tony Ryall, Belinda Vernon, Marie Hasler and David Carter from National, Doug Woolerton and Jenny Bloxham from New Zealand First, Rodney Hide from Act, Peter Dunne from United, John Wright from the Alliance and Michael Cullen and Ruth Dyson and Mark Peck from Labour.
The acceptance of nominations is normally a formality.

If they are approved, the government and the opposition will be evenly divided on the committee, although United's Peter Dunne and Act's Rodney Hide are likely to back the broad thrust of centre-right economic policy.
The committee itself elects the chair. National's Tony Ryall is tipped to win the FEC chairmanship.
Select committees scrutinise proposed legislation, hear submissions, examine departmental performance and can initiate their own inquiries.

The business committee has recommended the FEC be increased to 12 members from the normal eight. It has also recommended increasing the size of the Maori Affairs and Standing Orders committees to nine and the Government Administration, Health, Justice and Law Reform and Social Services committees to 10 members. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
